name: lean-check
description: Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
---

## Required proof loop

Load this skill before editing a Lean file. Before the first proof edit, invoke
at least one Lean LSP MCP query for the target (`lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal`). After every proof edit, invoke diagnostics or the goal query again
before starting another tactic attempt. Use `lean_multi_attempt`, hover, and
search to investigate candidates instead of repeatedly launching a build.

Do not start iterative proof work with `lake build`: it is a slow, final-boundary
check. Use LSP for the edit loop and reserve `lake build` for the final session
validation (or when a kernel check is specifically needed). When LSP is
unavailable or crashes, record that in the report and use the narrowest fallback,
usually `lake env lean <file>` or a single module, rather than silently skipping
the check.

LSP is sufficient between edits and between separate obligations. Do not run a
module build after every proof or repeat a narrow build immediately before a
configured final build that covers the same files. At the final boundary, run
the configured build once and wait for it. Add an earlier narrow kernel check
only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.

- During proof writing, prefer the Lean LSP MCP server for fast local feedback:
  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.
- Treat LSP feedback as interactive guidance, not final verification. The
  faithful check is Lean's kernel via the project build: run the configured
  build command, `lake build <Module>`, or `lake env lean <file>` from the
  project root.
- Prefer the project's configured build command when validating a task. Otherwise
  use the narrowest faithful check that covers the changed file/module.
- Re-run after each change and repair failures you introduce.
- Read errors top-down — the first error often causes the cascade. For each,
  note the `file:line`, expected vs actual type, and remaining goal.
- A `sorry` left in place is an open obligation, not a success. Do not hide a
  hard obligation behind a new `sorry` unless a hint explicitly allows it.

## Fast LSP proving loop

The `lean-lsp` MCP server gives sub-second feedback — far faster than a build
(10–30s+). Drive proofs with it, then confirm with the kernel. Key tools:

- `lean_goal(file, line)` — the proof state at a line. Call before writing any
  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit
  (`[]` = no errors, but *not* proof-complete — confirm with `lean_goal`).
- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.

Core loop: `lean_goal` (what to prove) → search a premise (see the `leansearch`
skill: `lean_local_search` / `lean_leansearch`) → `lean_multi_attempt` (test
candidates) → edit with the winner → `lean_diagnostic_messages` (confirm) →
kernel-check the module at the end.

## Heavy builds — actually wait for them

Read the WHOLE build output, not just pass/fail: warnings (unused variables,
deprecations, `sorry` notices, unexpected recompiles) are actionable — fix the
ones your change introduced, and record pre-existing/toolchain ones as memory
or an inbox issue rather than scrolling past (see the `horizon` skill,
"Warnings are work").

A cold `lake build` (or one that recompiles Mathlib) can take many minutes. The
most common way a session ends on a wrong conclusion is **not waiting for the
build to finish**:

- Do **not** assume you will be "automatically notified" or "re-invoked" when a
  background build completes — whether that happens depends entirely on the
  mechanism you used. If unsure, run the build in the **foreground** and block on
  it until it exits, then read the exit code.
- If you run it in the background, you MUST actively wait: poll its status/output
  until there is a definitive exit code (a monitor / until-loop, re-reading the
  log), and only then conclude. A background job you started but walked away from
  is *not* done.
- Scope the build to the narrowest faithful check (`lake build <Module>` or
  `lake env lean <file>`) to keep the wait short; reserve the full project build
  for final validation.
- Never write your final report — or `complete` an inbox item, or mark a task
  done — while a build that affects your conclusion is still running. If the
  engine cannot wait long enough, say so explicitly under `## Issues` and leave
  the next action clear, rather than implying the proof checked.
- Before marking a task or roadmap item done/blocked/rejected, add a concise
  closing comment with the exact check command, result, relevant files, and any
  caveat. If a task has `roadmap_refs`, make sure the linked roadmap items end
  with a consistent status and their own sync/closing comment.

## When the LSP dies on big import files

The Lean LSP loads the full environment for the file you open. On a file whose
imports pull in most of Mathlib (a broad `import Mathlib` umbrella, or a module
that transitively imports one), that environment is huge and the LSP server can
run out of memory or time out and die. This is an LSP limitation, **not** a
proof error:

- Do not treat an LSP crash/timeout on such a file as a failure of your proof.
  Fall back to the kernel check: `lake build <Module>` or `lake env lean <file>`,
  which verifies faithfully without holding the whole environment interactively.
- Prefer opening the **narrowest** module in the LSP. Avoid pointing the LSP at
  umbrella/`import Mathlib`-style files just to get feedback; edit and inspect
  the specific module you are proving in instead.
- If the LSP has crashed, restart it (or just proceed with `lake build`) rather
  than repeatedly reopening the same giant file and getting the same crash.

List-returning tools return an object with an `items` array. Empty = `{"items": []}`.

5. "What closes this goal?" -> lean_state_search
6. "What to feed simp?" -> lean_hammer_premise

After finding a name: lean_local_search to verify, lean_hover_info for signature.

## Return Formats
List-returning tools return an object with an `items` array. Empty = `{"items": []}`.

## Slow Files
On large files, pass `timeout_s` to lean_diagnostic_messages / lean_goal. A
response with `partial: true` + `still_elaborating_lines` (or goal `status:
'still_elaborating'`) means Lean is still working - poll again; it is NOT an
error or a dead server.

## Error Handling
Check `isError` in responses: `true` means failure (timeout/LSP error/rate limit), while an empty `items` with `isError: false` means no results found.

Run a code snippet and return diagnostics. Must include all imports.

}): Promise<CallToolResult<{

  // Whether code compiled successfully
  success: boolean;
  // True if elaboration timed out (results are partial)

```"}]

    46	/-! ## The δ ring diagram and its colimit `K = colim k''` -/
    47	
    48	section FieldColimit
    49	
    50	variable {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    51	
    52	/-- **The δ `CommRingCat` diagram.**  The finite subextensions `k''` of `K`, as commutative
    53	rings, with the field inclusions `k'' ↪ k'''` as transition maps.  Its filtered colimit is
    54	`K` (`deltaIsColimit`): the honest ring-level "`K = colim k''`". -/
    55	noncomputable def deltaRingDiagram : FinSubext k K ⥤ CommRingCat.{u} where
    56	  obj L := CommRingCat.of L.1
    57	  map {L₁ L₂} h := CommRingCat.ofHom (IntermediateField.inclusion (leOfHom h)).toRingHom
    58	  map_id L := by
    59	    apply CommRingCat.hom_ext
    60	    ext x
    61	    simp [IntermediateField.inclusion_self]
    62	  map_comp {L₁ L₂ L₃} f g := by
    63	    apply CommRingCat.hom_ext
    64	    ext x
    65	    simp [IntermediateField.inclusion_inclusion]
    66	
    67	/-- **The δ colimit cocone.**  The inclusion cocone from the finite subextensions to the
    68	whole field `K`, with `app k'' = k'' ↪ K`. -/
    69	noncomputable def deltaCocone : Cocone (deltaRingDiagram (k := k) (K := K)) where
    70	  pt := CommRingCat.of K
    71	  ι :=
    72	    { app := fun L => CommRingCat.ofHom (IntermediateField.val L.1).toRingHom
    73	      naturality := fun {L₁ L₂} h => by
    74	        apply CommRingCat.hom_ext
    75	        ext x
    76	        rfl }
    77	
    78	/-- **The δ colimit `K = colim k''` (ring level).**  The inclusion cocone `deltaCocone` is a
    79	colimit: `forget CommRingCat` reflects filtered colimits, and on underlying types the cocone
    80	is a filtered colimit by `Types.FilteredColimit.isColimitOf'` — joint surjectivity is the
    81	landed `coe_iSup_finSubext`/`iSup_finSubext_eq_top` (every `x : K` lives at a finite stage),
    82	and the injections are the field inclusions. -/
    83	noncomputable def deltaIsColimit [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K] :
    84	    IsColimit (deltaCocone (k := k) (K := K)) := by
    85	  haveI : ReflectsColimit (deltaRingDiagram (k := k) (K := K)) (forget CommRingCat.{u}) :=
    86	    reflectsColimit_of_reflectsIsomorphisms _ _
    87	  apply isColimitOfReflects (forget CommRingCat.{u})
    88	  refine Types.FilteredColimit.isColimitOf' _ _ ?_ ?_
    89	  · intro x
    90	    have hx : x ∈ ⋃ L : FinSubext k K, (L.1 : Set K) := by
    91	      rw [← coe_iSup_finSubext, iSup_finSubext_eq_top]; trivial
    92	    obtain ⟨L, hxL⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion.mp hx
    93	    exact ⟨L, ⟨x, hxL⟩, rfl⟩
    94	  · intro L x y hxy
    95	    exact ⟨L, 𝟙 L, by rw [show x = y from Subtype.ext hxy]⟩
    96	
    97	end FieldColimit

    99	/-! ## The δ scheme system `S : (FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Over (Spec k)` -/
   100	
   101	section SchemeSystem
   102	
   103	variable {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
   104	
   105	/-- The underlying scheme of `overSpec k A` is affine (it is `Spec A`). -/
   106	instance isAffine_overSpec_left (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :
   107	    IsAffine (overSpec k A).left :=
   108	  inferInstanceAs (IsAffine (Spec _))
   109	
   110	/-- The δ scheme transition morphism `Spec k''' ⟶ Spec k''` in `Over (Spec k)`, for
   111	`k'' ≤ k'''`: `Spec` of the field inclusion `k'' ↪ k'''`.  Well-defined over `Spec k`
   112	because the inclusion is a `k`-algebra map. -/
   113	noncomputable def deltaSchemeMap {L₁ L₂ : FinSubext k K} (h : L₁.1 ≤ L₂.1) :
   114	    overSpec k L₂.1 ⟶ overSpec k L₁.1 :=
   115	  Over.homMk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (IntermediateField.inclusion h).toRingHom)) (by
   116	    simp only [overSpec_left, Over.mk_hom, ← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
   117	    congr 2)
   118	
   119	@[simp]
   120	lemma deltaSchemeMap_left {L₁ L₂ : FinSubext k K} (h : L₁.1 ≤ L₂.1) :
   121	    (deltaSchemeMap h).left
   122	      = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (IntermediateField.inclusion h).toRingHom) :=
   123	  rfl
   124	
   125	/-- **The δ scheme diagram.**  `S.obj (op k'') = overSpec k k'' = Spec k''` over `Spec k`,
   126	with the transition maps `Spec` of the field inclusions.  Its limit is `Spec K = overSpec k K`
   127	(`deltaSchemeIsLimit`). -/
   128	noncomputable def deltaSchemeDiagram : (FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Over (Spec (.of k)) where
   129	  obj L := overSpec k (unop L).1
   130	  map {L₁ L₂} h := deltaSchemeMap (leOfHom h.unop)
   131	  map_id L := by
   132	    apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
   133	    simp only [deltaSchemeMap_left, Over.id_left, overSpec_left]
   134	    rw [← Spec.map_id]
   135	    congr 1
   136	  map_comp {L₁ L₂ L₃} f g := by
   137	    apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
   138	    simp only [Over.comp_left, deltaSchemeMap_left, overSpec_left, ← Spec.map_comp,
   139	      ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
   140	    congr 2
   141	
   142	@[simp]
   143	lemma deltaSchemeDiagram_map {L₁ L₂ : (FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ} (h : L₁ ⟶ L₂) :
   144	    deltaSchemeDiagram.map h = deltaSchemeMap (leOfHom h.unop) :=
   145	  rfl
   146	
   147	/-- Every δ transition map is affine (`Spec` of a field hom; both source and target are
   148	affine). -/
   149	instance deltaSchemeMap_isAffineHom {L₁ L₂ : FinSubext k K} (h : L₁.1 ≤ L₂.1) :
   150	    IsAffineHom (deltaSchemeMap h).left :=
   151	  isAffineHom_of_isAffine _
   152	
   153	/-- Every δ stage is a one-point (hence compact) space: `Spec` of a field. -/
   154	instance deltaSchemeDiagram_compactSpace (L : (FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ) :
   155	    CompactSpace ((deltaSchemeDiagram.obj L).left) :=
   156	  inferInstanceAs (CompactSpace (Spec _))
   157	
   158	/-- Every δ stage is quasi-separated: `Spec` of a field is affine. -/
   159	instance deltaSchemeDiagram_quasiSeparatedSpace (L : (FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ) :
   160	    QuasiSeparatedSpace ((deltaSchemeDiagram.obj L).left) :=
   161	  inferInstanceAs (QuasiSeparatedSpace (Spec _))
   162	
   163	end SchemeSystem

   165	/-! ## The δ scheme limit `Spec K = lim S` -/
   166	
   167	section SchemeLimit
   168	
   169	variable {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K]
   170	
   171	/-- `Scheme.Spec` is a right adjoint (`Γ ⊣ Spec`), so it preserves the δ cofiltered limit. -/
   172	noncomputable instance : PreservesLimitsOfShape (FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ Scheme.Spec.{u} :=
   173	  inferInstance
   174	
   175	omit [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K] in
   176	/-- **The δ bridge (definitional).**  Forgetting the base of the δ *scheme* diagram gives the
   177	δ *ring* diagram, opposite, under `Scheme.Spec`: both send `k'' ↦ Spec k''`. -/
   178	lemma deltaScheme_forget_eq :
   179	    deltaSchemeDiagram (k := k) (K := K) ⋙ Over.forget (Spec (.of k))
   180	      = deltaRingDiagram.op ⋙ Scheme.Spec := rfl
   181	
   182	/-- The forgotten δ scheme diagram (`k'' ↦ Spec k''` in `Scheme`) has a limit `Spec K`: it is
   183	`Scheme.Spec` of the δ ring colimit `deltaIsColimit` (opposite), and `Scheme.Spec` (right adjoint
   184	`Γ ⊣ Spec`) preserves limits.  This is the honest `Spec K_s = lim_{k''} Spec k''`. -/
   185	noncomputable instance hasLimit_deltaScheme_forget :
   186	    HasLimit (deltaSchemeDiagram (k := k) (K := K) ⋙ Over.forget (Spec (.of k))) := by
   187	  rw [deltaScheme_forget_eq]
   188	  exact ⟨_, isLimitOfPreserves Scheme.Spec deltaIsColimit.op⟩
   189	
   190	/-- **The δ scheme colimit `Spec K = lim S`.**  The δ scheme diagram `S` has a limit — `Spec K`:
   191	`Over.forget (Spec k)` *creates* limits of this (cofiltered ⟹ connected) shape, lifting the
   192	forgotten limit `Spec K = Scheme.Spec (colim_{k''} k'')` (`hasLimit_deltaScheme_forget`) uniquely
   193	to `Over (Spec k)`.  So the δ scheme system `S` is a legal input to the β1 residual
   194	`Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit`, and its limit is `Spec K_s`. -/
   195	noncomputable instance : HasLimit (deltaSchemeDiagram (k := k) (K := K)) := by
   196	  haveI : IsConnected (FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ := IsCofiltered.isConnected _
   197	  exact hasLimit_of_created (deltaSchemeDiagram (k := k) (K := K)) (Over.forget (Spec (.of k)))
   198	
   199	end SchemeLimit
   200	
   201	/-! ## The δ system plugs into the β1 residual, and the mountain
   202	
   203	`preservesColimit_deltaScheme_of_residual` closes the loop of deliverable 1: the concrete δ
   204	scheme system `deltaSchemeDiagram` (all its residual hypotheses — affine transition maps,
   205	compact and quasi-separated stages, `HasLimit`/`Spec K = lim S` — discharged above) **is a legal
   206	input** to the β1 residual `Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit C`, and feeding it in yields the
   207	concrete β1-at-`K_s` statement:
   208	
   209	> `pic0TypeFunctor C` sends `Spec K_s = lim_{k''} Spec k''` to the filtered colimit of its values,
   210	> i.e. `colim_{k''} pic0Subgroup C (Spec k'') → pic0Subgroup C (Spec K_s)` is a bijection.
   211	
   212	**The mountain (`Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit C`) is NOT discharged here** — it is the
   213	genuine M–L residual (landing notes I-0263/I-0266), stating that `pic0TypeFunctor C` is *locally
   214	of finite presentation as a functor*.  On affine tests `overSpec k A` it is exactly that
   215	`PicEtAff C A` (hence `pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)`) commutes with filtered colimits of the test
   216	algebra `A`, riding **finite presentation of the proper smooth curve `C/k`**: `C.hom` is
   217	`SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` (hence `LocallyOfFiniteType`/`LocallyOfFinitePresentation`) and
   218	`IsProper` (hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated), so `C.hom` is finitely presented.  The
   219	general (qcqs) case reduces to the affine one by spreading the affine opens and sections of
   220	`S_{K_s} = lim S_{k''}` back to a finite stage.  Named mathlib avatars (`v4.31.0`):
   221	`CommRingCat.preservesColimit_coyoneda_of_finitePresentation`
   222	(`Algebra/Category/Ring/FinitePresentation.lean:144`),
   223	`RingHom.EssFiniteType.exists_eq_comp_ι_app_of_isColimit` (`:81`) /
   224	`exists_comp_map_eq_of_isColimit` (`:45`),
   225	`Scheme.exists_π_app_comp_eq_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation`
   226	(`AlgebraicGeometry/AffineTransitionLimit.lean:1177`),
   227	`Scheme.exists_hom_hom_comp_eq_comp_of_locallyOfFiniteType` (`:686`),
   228	`Scheme.exists_isAffineOpen_preimage_eq` (`:1058`) / `exists_isOpenCover_and_isAffine` (`:1078`).
   229	-/
   230	
   231	section Residual
   232	
   233	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   234	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   235	variable (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K]
   236	
   237	/-- **The δ system plugs into the β1 residual.**  Given the β1 residual
   238	`Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit C` (the pinned M–L mountain), the concrete δ scheme system
   239	`deltaSchemeDiagram`, with all its residual hypotheses discharged (affine transition maps,
   240	compact and quasi-separated `Spec`-of-field stages, and `HasLimit`/`Spec K = lim S`), yields
   241	β1-at-`K_s`: `pic0TypeFunctor C` preserves the δ colimit
   242	`colim_{k''} pic0(Spec k'') → pic0(Spec K)`.  This is the honest consumption of the δ substrate
   243	by the residual, `divRep`-free. -/
   244	theorem preservesColimit_deltaScheme_of_residual
   245	    (h : Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit C) :
   246	    PreservesColimit (deltaSchemeDiagram (k := k) (K := K)).op (pic0TypeFunctor C) := by
   247	  apply h (deltaSchemeDiagram (k := k) (K := K))
   248	  · intro i j f
   249	    exact deltaSchemeMap_isAffineHom (leOfHom f.unop)
   250	  · intro i
   251	    exact deltaSchemeDiagram_compactSpace i
   252	  · intro i
   253	    exact deltaSchemeDiagram_quasiSeparatedSpace i
   254	
   255	end Residual
   256	
   257	end AlgebraicGeometry.DatG0

/-!
# Base change of the final finite-stage Picard atlas

The glue package extends the finite-presentation models from `M` to a final finite
subextension `N`.  Extending once more to the separably closed field cancels the tower
`M -> N -> k`.  The resulting component equivalences recover the exact Picard atlas
rings and intertwine every restriction and transition map.
-/

universe u

open CategoryTheory TensorProduct
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

noncomputable section

variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]

    11	/-!
    12	# The tensor-overlap comparison for Picard representability
    13	
    14	For a field extension `k → L`, the two coprojections
    15	`L → L ⊗[k] L` induce two pullbacks of an L-side representation.  This file
    16	constructs the comparison between those two representing schemes.  Each pullback
    17	is obtained from `Over.mapPullbackAdj`; the presheaf comparison is assembled from
    18	the landed theta isomorphism and the equality of the two composites back to `k`.
    19	
    20	Over the triple tensor product, the three actual Amitsur faces determine three maps
    21	back to `Spec L`.  The corresponding Picard comparisons are defined independently
    22	through a common k-side functor, and Yoneda uniqueness turns their natural-isomorphism
    23	cocycle into the representing-scheme cocycle.  In particular, the `1,3` comparison is
    24	not defined as the composite of the other two.
    25	-/

    43	/-- The first map `Spec (L ⊗[k] L) ⟶ Spec L`. -/

    47	    (tensorInl (k := k) (A := k) (B := L)).toRingHom)
    48	
    49	/-- The second map `Spec (L ⊗[k] L) ⟶ Spec L`. -/
    50	noncomputable def tensorOverlapInr :
    51	    Spec (.of (L ⊗[k] L)) ⟶ Spec (.of L) :=
    52	  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
    53	    (tensorInr (k := k) (A := k) (B := L)).toRingHom)
    54	
    55	/-- The common map to `Spec k` obtained from either tensor coprojection. -/
    56	noncomputable def tensorOverlapBase :
    57	    Spec (.of L) ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
    58	  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))

    65	  rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← Spec.map_comp]

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0FiniteStageRightLegEquality.lean
+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
+-/
+import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
+
+/-!
+# The right leg of the finite-stage Picard glue datum
+
+The transition from the reversed overlap carries its left restriction to the
+right restriction of the forward overlap.  This file reflects that identity to
+the finite stage and then extends it to the final finite subextension.
+-/
+
+set_option autoImplicit false
+
+universe u
+
+open CategoryTheory TensorProduct
+open scoped TensorProduct
+
+namespace AlgebraicGeometry
+
+noncomputable section
+
+variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
+variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
+  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [IsSepClosed k]
+
+namespace Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
+
+/-- On the exact Picard atlas, transition from the reversed overlap followed
+by its left restriction is the right restriction of the forward overlap. -/
+theorem transition_comp_restrictionLeft_eq_restrictionRight
+    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
+    (pic0FiniteStageTransition C (U, V)).comp
+        (pic0FiniteStageRestrictionLeft C V U) =
+      pic0FiniteStageRestrictionRight C U V := by
+  apply DFunLike.ext _ _
+  intro x
+  let J := (pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1
+  letI : J.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := ⟨J.hom⟩
+  let hLeft : V.1.1 ⊓ U.1.1 ≤ V.1.1 :=
+    pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap_le_left C V U
+  let hTransition : U.1.1 ⊓ V.1.1 ≤ V.1.1 ⊓ U.1.1 := by
+    rw [inf_comm]
+  let hRight : U.1.1 ⊓ V.1.1 ≤ V.1.1 :=
+    pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap_le_right C U V
+  change (J.left.resHom hTransition) ((J.left.resHom hLeft) x) =
+    (J.left.resHom hRight) x
+  calc
+    _ = (J.left.resHom (hTransition.trans hLeft)) x :=
+      Scheme.resHom_resHom hLeft hTransition x
+    _ = (J.left.resHom hRight) x := by rfl
+
+/-- The exact right-leg equation transported to the ambient tensor-product
+models used by the finite-stage package. -/
+theorem transportedMap_transition_comp_restrictionLeft_eq_right
+    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
+    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F)
+    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
+    (pic0FiniteStageTransportedMap C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.e
+        (Sum.inr (U, V))).comp
+        (pic0FiniteStageTransportedMap C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.e
+          (Sum.inl (Sum.inl (V, U)))) =
+      pic0FiniteStageTransportedMap C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.e
+        (Sum.inl (Sum.inr (U, V))) := by
+  have hExact := transition_comp_restrictionLeft_eq_restrictionRight C U V
+  apply DFunLike.ext _ _
+  intro x
+  change
+    (P.e (Sum.inr (U, V))).symm
+      (pic0FiniteStageTransition C (U, V)
+        ((P.e (Sum.inr (V, U)))
+          ((P.e (Sum.inr (V, U))).symm
+            (pic0FiniteStageRestrictionLeft C V U ((P.e (Sum.inl V)) x))))) =
+    (P.e (Sum.inr (U, V))).symm
+      (pic0FiniteStageRestrictionRight C U V ((P.e (Sum.inl V)) x))
+  rw [(P.e (Sum.inr (V, U))).apply_symm_apply]
+  exact congrArg (P.e (Sum.inr (U, V))).symm
+    (DFunLike.congr_fun hExact ((P.e (Sum.inl V)) x))
+
+/-- The descended transition followed by the descended reversed left
+restriction is the descended forward right restriction. -/
+theorem mapM_transition_comp_restrictionLeft_eq_right
+    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
+    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F)
+    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
+    (P.mapM (Sum.inr (U, V))).comp
+        (P.mapM (Sum.inl (Sum.inl (V, U)))) =
+      P.mapM (Sum.inl (Sum.inr (U, V)) := by
+  apply DatG0.tensorProduct_algHom_comp_eq_of_baseChange P.M
+    (P.mapM (Sum.inl (Sum.inl (V, U))))
+    (P.mapM (Sum.inr (U, V)))
+    (P.mapM (Sum.inl (Sum.inr (U, V))))
+    (pic0FiniteStageTransportedMap C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.e
+      (Sum.inl (Sum.inl (V, U))))
+    (pic0FiniteStageTransportedMap C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.e
+      (Sum.inr (U, V)))
+    (pic0FiniteStageTransportedMap C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.e
+      (Sum.inl (Sum.inr (U, V))))
+  · exact P.hmapM _
+  · exact P.hmapM _
+  · exact P.hmapM _
+  · exact transportedMap_transition_comp_restrictionLeft_eq_right C P U V
+
+/-- After scalar extension to the package's final finite subextension, the
+transition followed by the reversed left restriction is the forward right leg. -/
+theorem transitionBaseChange_comp_restrictionBaseChange_eq_right
+    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
+    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F)
+    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
+    (pic0FiniteStageTransitionBaseChange
+      C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.mapM P.N U V).comp
+      (pic0FiniteStageRestrictionBaseChange
+        C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.mapM P.N V U) =
+    AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := P.M.1) (K := P.N.1)
+      (P.mapM (Sum.inl (Sum.inr (U, V)))) := by
+  change
+    (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := P.M.1) (K := P.N.1)
+      (P.mapM (Sum.inr (U, V)))).comp
+      (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := P.M.1) (K := P.N.1)
+        (P.mapM (Sum.inl (Sum.inl (V, U))))) =
+    AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := P.M.1) (K := P.N.1)
+      (P.mapM (Sum.inl (Sum.inr (U, V))))
+  rw [AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom_comp,
+    mapM_transition_comp_restrictionLeft_eq_right C P U V]
+
+end Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
+
+end
+
+end AlgebraicGeometry
*** End Patch";
const result = await tools.apply_patch(patch);
text(typeof result === "string" ? result : JSON.stringify(result));
